videos.script: Lesson 1 built an API that works. This lesson makes it one that other programs can rely on. {{contract}} A client never sees your code. It sees the JSON you send, and it is written against every detail of it. So the details are the contract. {{types}} A price sent as a float loses a cent. An id that is too large arrives as a different number. A time with no offset names two different moments. {{shapes}} Errors are part of the contract too. A program cannot read a sentence, so the error has to be data it can branch on. {{problem}} Then the list of books grows. You split it into pages, and you see why counting positions skips a book when somebody adds one. {{pages}} And on a bad network a client sends the same request twice. A key in a header makes the second one harmless. {{keys}} At the end you will know which changes your clients can absorb, and which ones break them without a single error. {{compat}}
